title: Host refuses test credit for watcher events on files whose bytes and mtimes predate the run (two occurrences 2026-10-24)
outcome: Host refuses test credit for watcher events on files whose bytes and mtimes predate the run (two occurrences 2026-10-24)
acceptance: RED-first regressions demonstrate that directory-only metadata notifications for an existing plain directory such as .claude do not by themselves refuse an otherwise unchanged launcher run; the tests exercise the watcher-to-credit path, and genuine child-file events remain observable.

Real source mutations remain fail-closed: edits (including write-then-restore), creation, deletion or rename of tracked .claude files and other source files still refuse credit, and a directory replacement, symlink/reparse point or unknown/unreadable path is not granted the metadata-only exemption. No blanket .claude ignore and no final-hash-only waiver is introduced.

The change is delivered as a frozen patch with focused watcher/carried-check regressions passing on that exact source and a fresh read-only Codex+Claude pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding. The item records the incident evidence, the tested mechanism, and whether the Claude-runtime-writer hypothesis was established or remains unproven; full landing gate and integration remain Merger's responsibility. The item also states, for each of the four recorded occurrences, whether this change explains it; the file-level may-write refusals on source files (occurrences 2 and 3) are split into their own item if not explained.
